text.p: Cars queued for hours at filling stations in Lagos on Monday as a fuel shortage blamed on a row between two federal agencies gripped oil-producing Nigeria's commercial hub.
"The situation is unbearable," said bus driver Jimoh Ladipo, who had waited in a queue for five hours without getting any fuel. Queues stretched for several hundred metres (yards).
Oil industry sources blamed the shortage on a dispute between the state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) and the port authority over debts owed each other.
Oil Minister Dan Etete, on a visit to Lagos from the capital Abuja, said on Monday there was no reason for fuel to be scarce in the sprawling city.
"As of today we have vessels discharging over 10,000 metric tonnes of fuel in the Lagos area," he told state radio.
Last week there was a shortage of aviation fuel in Lagos because the port authority refused to handle NNPC vessels bringing the product from Port Harcourt refinery in the southeast.
NNPC, which says it is also owed for its services by the port authority, said the dispute had been resolved.
Etete said a committee would be set up to determine the two agencies' outstanding debts to each other in order to resolve the issue once and for all.
Fuel supplies, often erratic in the West African nation, had been relatively stable since the last major shortage in March last year.
